testimonials.name: Dr. Meera Iyer
testimonials.quote: Keep a pot of basil on the windowsill. A few fresh leaves in salads and soups add flavor without salt, plus antioxidants and vitamin K.

testimonials.name: Dr. Daniel Okafor
testimonials.quote: A cup of fresh mint tea after dinner can calm mild indigestion and bloating thanks to its cooling menthol. Go gently if you get acid reflux.

testimonials.name: Dr. Sofia Marchetti
testimonials.quote: A lavender sachet by the pillow and a warm cup of tea make a calming bedtime routine. Never swallow the essential oil.

testimonials.name: Dr. Arjun Rao
testimonials.quote: Rub rosemary on roast vegetables for flavor and antioxidants. Its fresh scent helps many people feel alert. Avoid medicinal doses in pregnancy.

testimonials.name: Dr. Helen Brooks
testimonials.quote: Honey-sweetened thyme tea is an old comfort for a scratchy throat or cough. Thymol has antibacterial properties. See your doctor if a cough lingers.

testimonials.name: Dr. Karel Novak
testimonials.quote: Fry sage in brown butter, or use a cooled infusion as a sore-throat gargle. Stick to food and tea amounts, and avoid medicinal doses in pregnancy.

testimonials.name: Dr. Priya Shah
testimonials.quote: A warm cup of chamomile in the evening helps many people unwind and can ease an upset stomach. Check first if you are allergic to ragweed or daisies.

testimonials.name: Tomas Lindqvist
testimonials.quote: Snip chives over eggs or potatoes for flavor with almost no calories, plus vitamins K and C. Keep the pot away from cats and dogs.
